Start a circular layout

Source: R/ggcircos.R
ggcircos.Rd

Creates the plot that every other ggcircos layer attaches to. The layout – node arcs, sectors and the angular slot reserved for each link – is computed once, here, and stored as data; it is never modified afterwards. ggcircos() itself adds no layer, so you can draw links, node arcs, labels and outer tracks in any order.

Usage

ggcircos(
  data,
  nodes = NULL,
  sectors = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  layout = c("circular", "arc"),
  gap = 0.01,
  sector_gap = 0.05,
  slot_fill = 0.9,
  slot_gap = NULL,
  start = 0,
  tracks = NULL,
  track_offset = 0.06,
  self_loops = FALSE,
  radius = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A square matrix, a data.frame with from/to columns, a tidygraph/igraph object, or an existing circos_layout.

nodes, sectors, order, gap, sector_gap, slot_fill, start, tracks, track_offset, self_loops

Passed to circos_layout(), which documents each of them.

layout

"circular" for the polar layout, "arc" for the linear one, where links bulge to the left of a vertical spine.

slot_gap

Absolute seam in radians between adjacent link slots, the way circlize::chordDiagram()'s diffHeight is a fixed height. NULL uses the slot_fill fraction; a fixed value keeps ribbons visibly separate when a node carries many links.

radius

Base radius of the node ring. ggcircos() derives this from layout; you rarely need to set it.

weight

Name of the column holding each link's weight, e.g. weight = r or weight = "r" (a matrix supplies r). Set it to make the layout carry the values the way circlize::chordDiagram() does: node arcs proportional to the weight they carry, slots proportional to their link's weight. Left NULL every node keeps an equal arc and the values only drive aes(fill = ).

columns

Optional named character vector mapping the layout's column names onto your data's, e.g. c(from = "qaccver", to = "saccver") for BLAST table output. The rename is a copy; columns you do not map travel with the link table, so weight = and aes() can still reach them.

by

Name of a node-table column to lay out one ring per group of its values (spec sec.9.1, the facet "B-plan"). Each panel gets its own node subset and its own ordering; finish with facet_wrap(~ <the same column>). A link whose two ends fall in different groups is dropped with a message, since it belongs to no single ring. NULL (the default) builds one shared layout, the A-plan.

...

Passed on to circos_layout().

Value

A ggplot with a ggcircos layout attached.

See also

geom_chord(), geom_node_arc(), geom_track()

Examples

ggcircos(cor(mtcars), order = "hclust") +
    geom_chord(aes(fill = r)) +
    geom_node_arc() +
    geom_node_text()


# two genomes in two sectors
nodes <- data.frame(
    id = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
    genome = c("ref", "ref", "qry", "qry"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
links <- data.frame(
    from = c("a", "c"), to = c("d", "b"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ggcircos(links, nodes = nodes, sectors = "genome") +
    geom_chord() +
    geom_node_arc()
